notes:
Summary: Mid-market SaaS (product analytics) evaluating Redwood Hosted first; successful 14-day trial, now moving to Dedicated sizing and traffic forecast. Short, actionable CRM notes below.

Hosted trial highlights (14 days):
- Total tokens used: ~1.2M (includes both prompts + completions).
- Average QPS observed: 5.9 (steady-state), peak observed burst: 24 QPS (30s spikes).
- Average concurrency during peak windows: 8-12 concurrent requests.
- Token length mix: ~35% short completions (~40-120 tokens), ~55% medium (~200-400 tokens), ~10% long-form (>1200 tokens for generation workflows).
- Embeddings: ~60k vectors generated across the trial; typical batch size 32; embeddings pipeline has spikes during nightly doc ingestion windows.
- Reranking: low QPS but CPU-heavy; batched rerank jobs run in background.
- Observed p95 latency on Hosted (default routing): ~320ms for chat completions (model = open-llama-like / curated), p50 ~110ms.

Business needs + constraints:
- Primary apps: customer-facing chat assistant (SLA critical), in-product doc search (embeddings + reranking), feature suggestion system (rerank + prompt engineering).
- Latency SLO: target p95 < 200ms for chat in EU/US regions; occasional degradation acceptable during rollouts but want predictable fallbacks.
- Throughput target for Dedicated: forecast growth to sustained 60 QPS within 12 months, headroom for 200+ QPS bursts during product launches.
- Cost sensitivity: aiming to keep inference unit economics < $0.02 per active user/month on average; careful about per-token spend during heavy generation.
- Security/compliance: need SSO (SAML), SOC2 attestation, audit logs retention 12+ months, optional KMS integration for key control; data residency preference: US + EU.

Dedicated capacity ask (what Sales/SE to deliver):
- Produce a Dedicated sizing guideline mapping current Hosted metrics -> GPU pool sizing + autoscale rules. Key vars: baseline concurrency 8-12, steady QPS 60 (future), peak bursts 200 QPS for <5 minutes.
- Provide cost model: monthly committed vs. burst pricing; expected token/cost breakdown (generation vs. embeddings vs. rerank).
- Propose routing policy: primary US cluster (Dedicated), fallback to lower-cost regional variants for non-critical workloads, embeddings routed to separate pool to avoid interference.

Initial SE recommendations (from Riya):
- Baseline Dedicated cluster: 3 x mid-range GPUs (e.g., 80GB class equivalent) to serve steady-state 60 QPS with ~18 concurrency per GPU; autoscale to 6 GPUs for sustained high throughput.
- For heavy generation (long-form tokens) isolate on 1-2 dedicated nodes with higher memory to keep latency predictable.
- Embeddings: separate autoscaling pool sized for batch throughput (recommend 2 x medium GPUs + burst to 4 during ingestion).
- Suggested concurrency caps + continuous batching knobs to control latency vs cost.

Next steps (short):
- AE Alex to send Dedicated sizing + cost deck (drive link above) by 2026-03-12.
- SE Riya to run synthetic load test template and align on QPS/concurrency assumptions prior to POC.
- Security to complete questionnaire; assign Redwood security engineer for 1:1 review.
